introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), June 2019, ADVANCED LEVEL. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure considered as an attempt to cheat will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorized composition will earn you no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION C: PRESCRIBED TEXT (20 marks)**

Answer ONE question only.

questions.enonce_markdown: **4)** Show how writers use pathos to foster understanding of their works using any three prescribed texts.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Method answer: the prescribed texts are not available here, so no detail of any work is given. Apply this method to the three texts you have studied.**

**Understanding the question**

- "pathos": the quality in a work that arouses pity, sympathy, sorrow or indignation in the reader (an appeal to emotion).
- "how writers use": the techniques (the means): suffering of innocent or sympathetic characters, tragic events, vivid imagery, tone and diction, first-person voice, irony, setting, dramatic situations, contrast.
- "to foster understanding of their works": the purpose: emotion is used to make the reader grasp the theme or message (injustice, loss, cruelty, resilience), so every point must link technique, emotion and meaning.
- "any three prescribed texts": exactly three.

**Plan**

1. Introduction: define pathos, name the three texts and state the thesis: the writers move the reader in order to make him or her understand their themes.
2. Body, ORGANISED BY TECHNIQUE (or by text): for each technique, an example from each text (a scene, a character, a short quotation), the emotion it creates and the understanding it brings.
3. A paragraph on the effect on the reader: sympathy that changes attitudes and leads to reflection on the issues of the text.
4. Conclusion: judgement on how essential pathos is to the meaning of the works.

**Opening pattern**: "Pathos is the power of a work to move its readers to pity and sympathy. In [Text A], [Text B] and [Text C], the writers use [technique] and [technique] so that the reader may understand..."

**Marking grid (indicative; the paper prints only 20 marks)**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Relevance and argument | Pathos defined and always linked to understanding of the work |
| Knowledge of the texts | Precise scenes and techniques from three texts |
| Organisation | Clear paragraphs, introduction, conclusion |
| Expression and accuracy | Formal register, correct grammar and spelling |

**Common mistakes**

1. Retelling sad events without naming the technique or explaining the effect on the reader.
2. Confusing pathos with pity for the writer, or never saying what the emotion helps the reader to understand.

incertitudes: Consigne de la page de garde (règle de choix) : « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet ». Section A obligatoire (aucune règle), Section B : 1 sujet sur 6 (a à f), Section C : 1 question sur 4. Les regles_choix sont identiques dans les 12 fichiers.

Fautes imprimées dans le sujet, laissées telles quelles : titre « SECTION A SUMMERY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION » (summary), « for few hours » (Q1), « A this stage », « into the will » (mill), « The stripped cane are then », « out of them » (Q2, forme reconstruite) ; Section C question 2 : « Use any Three prescribed text ».
Le tiret cadratin du passage de résumé (« choice of home - among the stinging tentacles ») est écrit « - » conformément à la règle du projet. Le passage ne porte pas de numéros de ligne imprimés.

Section A : le sujet imprime 30 marks pour la section (15 par question). La répartition des 15 points du résumé n'est pas imprimée : la grille du corrigé est indicative. La reconstruction est comptée à 1 point par blanc (15 blancs), ce qui est une hypothèse ; plusieurs réponses sont acceptables pour certains blancs (voir le corrigé).

Section B : 20 marks (Content and Organisation 6, Expression 8, Accuracy 6), 500 à 550 mots demandés. Points imprimés non corrigés. Compositions modèles : comptes de mots faits par script (de 517 à 534 mots).

Section C question 4 : corrigé de méthode : œuvre non disponible. Les textes au programme ne sont pas fournis ; aucun détail d'intrigue, de personnage ni de citation n'est donné, le corrigé indique la démarche, le plan et les critères. Chaque question vaut 20 marks (imprimé).
